sections.title: Growth & Margins
sections.subtitle: Revenue reaccelerated after a flat FY2018–FY2023 stretch (~€34–38bn); Q3 is structurally the biggest quarter on Northern-hemisphere flu shipments, so read quarterly bars YoY, never QoQ.

charts.title: Gross Margin
charts.annotation: Stepped up from ~70% (through FY2021) to 76-77% (FY2022-2025) on the EUROAPI spin-off and Opella divestiture, then to 79-81% in recent quarters as Dupixent's mix weight grows.

charts.title: Operating Margin
charts.annotation: FY rows are IFRS operating margin, which is noisy: FY2020's 39.2% includes the Regeneron stake disposal gain; FY2019's 8.4% is depressed by one-offs. Quarterly rows carry Sanofi's non-GAAP business operating margin instead (the cleaner series management guides on) — Q2-2026 was 28.4%, +3.7pp YoY. Q3 quarters run structurally highest on flu-vaccine seasonality (35.6-35.7% in Q3-2024/2025); always compare a quarter YoY, never to the adjacent quarter.

sections.title: Earnings & Cash Generation
sections.subtitle: EPS basis changes between annual and quarterly rows — see the EPS chart note before comparing across the FY/quarter toggle.

charts.title: EPS: IFRS (Annual) vs Business (Quarterly)
charts.annotation: CAUTION: FY rows are IFRS basic EPS, distorted by disposal gains — FY2020 €9.82 (Regeneron stake sale) and FY2025 €6.40 (Opella gain) both overstate the operating trend; FY2019's €2.24 is a genuine trough. Quarterly rows are business EPS (Sanofi's non-GAAP measure, the one management guides on) — FY2025 business EPS was €7.83 vs €6.40 IFRS. These are NOT one continuous comparable series; do not read a straight line across the FY/quarter toggle.

charts.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow
charts.annotation: Net income here is IFRS and carries the same disposal noise as the EPS chart (FY2020, FY2025). FreeCashFlow is statutory OCF less capex; FY2025 was €7,212m vs the company's own broader ‘free cash flow’ definition (pre-restructuring/acquisitions/disposals) of €9.9bn.

charts.title: Reported FCF vs Owner FCF (DCF Basis)
charts.annotation: Single FY2025 snapshot from the DCF JSON, not a CSV time series. Owner FCF (€6,899m) is the DCF's base and sits below both reported FCF (€7,212m) and the company's own broader FCF definition (€9,900m, which excludes restructuring/M&A/disposal cash flows the DCF treats as real costs).

charts.title: Shareholders' Equity
charts.annotation: Fell to €71,376m in FY2025 from €77,507m despite a profitable year — roughly €12bn was spent on BD/M&A (Blueprint Medicines, Vigil Neuroscience) and €5bn on buybacks, both charged directly against equity.

sections.title: Capital Allocation
sections.subtitle: A shrinking share count and a 31-year dividend growth streak are both part of the equity story, not just the income statement.

charts.title: Shares Outstanding
charts.annotation: Declining from 1,263m (FY2023) to 1,196.6m (Q2-2026) on buybacks (€5bn completed 2025, €1bn 2026 tranche completed by end-April), roughly 2-3%/year of dilution offset.

charts.title: Dividend Per Share
charts.annotation: €2.85 (FY2015) to €3.92 (FY2025) — a 31-year consecutive increase streak, with a 32nd expected for FY2026.

charts.title: Stock-Based Compensation
charts.annotation: SBC is only ~0.7% of revenue (€313m FY2025) — nearly an SBC-zero name by tech standards, which is why the DCF's house/street valuation band is unusually narrow (~€4.7/share wide).

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Total group net sales across Pharma (Immunology, Rare Disease, Neurology, Oncology) and Vaccines.

For Sanofi: FY2025 revenue was €43,626m, +9.9% at constant exchange rates, after a flat FY2018–FY2023 stretch around €34-38bn. H1-2026 accelerated further to +15.7%, and management upgraded FY2026 guidance to ~10% CER sales growth (from high-single-digit) at the July 2026 update.

What to watch:

  • Dupixent is ~36% of group sales and the majority of recent growth — its 2030 sales ambition was raised to ~€25bn (from ~€22bn) in July 2026
  • Q3 is structurally the largest quarter (Northern-hemisphere flu vaccine shipments, e.g. €12,434m in Q3-2025 vs €9,994m in Q2-2025) — always compare quarters YoY, never QoQ
  • General Medicines/legacy products are in structural decline, masking underlying growth in the headline consolidated number

grossMargin.title: Gross Margin
grossMargin.content:
Gross profit (revenue less cost of sales) as a percentage of revenue.

For Sanofi: stepped up materially from ~70% through FY2021 to 76-77% in FY2022-2025 (EUROAPI spin-off in 2022 removed lower-margin API manufacturing; the Opella Consumer Healthcare divestiture in Dec-2024 removed lower-margin OTC business), and further to 79-81% in the most recent quarters (81.2% in Q2-2026) as high-margin Dupixent grows as a share of the mix.

What to watch:

  • Whether the margin can keep climbing as Dupixent's own mix shifts toward more price pressure and gross-to-net deductions, which management already flagged for 2025
  • The post-2019 launch cohort (Ayvakit, ALTUVIIIO, Sarclisa, Wayrilz) is a smaller, generally lower-margin-at-launch group that could offset some of the Dupixent-driven lift over time

operatingMargin.title: Operating Margin
operatingMargin.content:
Operating income divided by revenue. Basis changes between rows: annual (FY) rows are IFRS operating margin; quarterly rows are Sanofi's non-GAAP business operating margin — the cleaner series management actually guides on.

For Sanofi: the annual IFRS series is noisy — FY2020's 39.2% includes the Regeneron equity stake disposal gain (operating income €14,113m that year), while FY2019's 8.4% is depressed by impairments and one-offs (operating income only €3,051m). Quarterly business operating margin was 28.4% in Q2-2026, +3.7pp YoY on gross-margin mix and cost discipline, with Q3 running structurally highest each year (35.6-35.7% in Q3-2024/2025) on flu-vaccine seasonality.

What to watch:

  • Always compare a quarter to the same quarter a year earlier, never to the adjacent quarter — the Q2-to-Q3 step-up is seasonal, not a margin inflection
  • Management is guiding to continued business-margin expansion under new CEO Belén Garijo’s ‘sustained profitable growth with increased focus on cash generation’ framing
  • Do not draw a trend line across the FY/quarter toggle as if this were one continuous series

eps.title: Earnings Per Share
eps.content:
Basis changes between rows in this chart — annual (FY) rows are IFRS basic EPS; quarterly rows are Sanofi's non-GAAP business EPS.

For Sanofi: IFRS EPS is repeatedly distorted by one-off disposal gains — FY2020 €9.82 (Regeneron stake sale) and FY2025 €6.40 (Opella divestiture gain) both overstate the operating trend, while FY2019's €2.24 is a genuine operating trough, not a comparable low. Business EPS (the metric management actually guides on) was €7.83 for FY2025, materially different from the €6.40 IFRS figure for the same year, and grew +33.3% YoY to €2.09 in Q2-2026.

What to watch:

  • Never draw a trend line across the FY/quarter toggle as if this were one continuous series — the two bases measure different things
  • FY2026 guidance calls for business EPS growth 'slightly faster than sales' (~10% CER), with an estimated ~-2% FX drag at July-2026 rates

niVsFcf.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow
niVsFcf.content:
IFRS net income compared against reported free cash flow (operating cash flow less capex).

For Sanofi: net income carries the same one-off disposal distortions as the EPS chart (FY2020 Regeneron gain, FY2025 Opella gain). FY2025 free cash flow was €7,212m; the company's own broader 'free cash flow' definition, which excludes restructuring, acquisition and disposal cash flows, was €9.9bn for the same year.

What to watch:

  • The gap between net income and FCF in disposal years (FY2020, FY2025) is the clearest visual flag that IFRS net income is not a clean read on the underlying business that year

ownerFcf.title: Reported FCF vs Owner FCF (DCF Basis)
ownerFcf.content:
A single FY2025 snapshot, sourced from the DCF JSON rather than the CSV time series, comparing three different free-cash-flow definitions.

For Sanofi: reported statutory FCF (OCF less capex) was €7,212m. The company's own broader definition (excluding restructuring, acquisition and disposal cash flows) was €9,900m. The DCF's owner FCF — the actual base for the valuation — is €6,899m, built from business EBITDA less D&A, capex and working capital, net of the full SBC charge, so it ties to a genuinely distributable cash figure rather than a management-adjusted one.

What to watch:

  • Owner-FCF margin history: 21.8% (FY2021, FY2022) down to 13.7% (FY2024, Opella separation costs plus a capex ramp) and back to 15.8% (FY2025) — the 3-year owner-FCF CAGR is negative even though revenue grew, driven by the US-onshoring capex ramp (€2.1bn FY2021 → €3.5bn FY2025) and elevated restructuring, both modelled explicitly in the DCF rather than extrapolated

equity.title: Shareholders' Equity
equity.content:
Total shareholders' equity at each fiscal year end.

For Sanofi: equity fell to €71,376m in FY2025 from €77,507m despite a profitable year, because roughly €12bn was deployed on BD/M&A (Blueprint Medicines, Vigil Neuroscience) and €5bn on buybacks — both charged directly against the balance sheet rather than flowing through the income statement.

What to watch:

  • Net debt rose from €8.8bn to €11.0bn over 2025 even after ~€10.4bn of Opella disposal proceeds, for the same reason — Sanofi intends to retain its Aa3/AA credit ratings but has less balance-sheet slack than before the Opella sale

shares.title: Shares Outstanding
shares.content:
Weighted-average shares outstanding used in EPS calculations.

For Sanofi: declining from 1,263m at FY2023 to 1,196.6m at Q2-2026, roughly 2-3% per year, funded by ongoing buybacks (€5bn completed in 2025, a €1bn 2026 tranche completed by end-April).

What to watch:

  • The DCF holds the share count flat at the current 1,196.6m rather than projecting continued buyback-driven decline — explicitly conservative, since SBC (only 0.7% of revenue) is fully expensed in the flows and charging further buyback-funded reduction on top would effectively double-count the capital return

dividend.title: Dividend Per Share
dividend.content:
Annual dividend declared per share.

For Sanofi: grown from €2.85 (FY2015) to €3.92 (FY2025) — a 31-year consecutive increase streak, one of the longest in European large-cap pharma, with a 32nd increase expected for FY2026.

What to watch:

  • The dividend has been sustained through a period (FY2018-2023) of largely flat revenue, so the streak reflects capital-allocation discipline as much as underlying growth — worth watching whether the post-Opella capital deployment toward M&A (€12bn in 2025) changes that priority

sbc.title: Stock-Based Compensation
sbc.content:
Share-based payment expense as reported in the consolidated cash flow statement add-back.

For Sanofi: €313m in FY2025, only about 0.7% of revenue — far below the 10-15% typical of US technology comparables. Sanofi's plans are predominantly performance shares settled with treasury shares, and no separate net-share-settlement tax line is disclosed, so the DCF takes the full cash flow add-back as the SBC charge.

What to watch:

  • Because SBC is so small, the DCF's house (fully-SBC-expensed) valuation and a looser street basis sit unusually close together — only about €4.7/share apart at the weighted intrinsic value — so this is nearly an SBC-neutral valuation call for Sanofi, unlike most tech dashboards on this platform

dcf.base_sublabel: Owner FCF — business EBITDA less D&A, capex, working capital and full SBC charge
dcf.growth_hint: Base-case Year-1 revenue growth (FY2026 upgraded guidance, ~9% reported after FX)
dcf.current_price_note: 2 days after verified live price (28-Aug-2026 close)
dcf.current_price_note_2: Terminal value is patent-cliff-constrained: 10-year explicit window ramps to ~€56bn sales by 2030 then turns revenue negative for 2032-2034 as Dupixent's US patents approach expiry, before capitalizing at 1.0-2.0% terminal growth with a 12-15x FCF cap that binds in all three scenarios.
